title: Adaptive Learning for Weakly Labeled Streams

problem.claim: Learning from continuously collected data streams is difficult when only a limited subset is labeled and those labels may be noisy.

gap.claim: Weakly labeled data streams are important and challenging but have rarely been studied.

contributions.claim: A noise transition matrix estimation approach for data streams with scarce noisy labels using online anchor point identification.
An adaptive learning algorithm for weakly labeled data streams based on model reuse and unlabeled data to alleviate the influence of label noise.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe the noise transition matrix estimation approach as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that theoretical analysis and extensive experiments justify and validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

narrative_sequence.summary: Real-world data are often collected as streams, while accurate labels are difficult to obtain.
The paper studies continuously collected data streams with limited, potentially noisy labels.
The setting is important but rarely studied, and unknown label noise makes generalization difficult.
The authors estimate noise transition matrices through online anchor point identification and use model reuse with unlabeled data in an adaptive learning algorithm.
The authors report support from theoretical analysis and extensive experiments.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not describe the theoretical assumptions or guarantees.
The abstract does not identify the types or rates of label noise handled.
